question: Who among the following wrote the biography of Jahangir known as Iqbalnama-i Jahangiri?
solution:
**The correct answer is - Mutamid Khan**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mutamid Khan**

 
 
• Mutamid Khan authored the biography of Jahangir known as "Iqbalnama-i Jahangiri".
 
• The work provides detailed accounts and chronicles of the reign of Emperor Jahangir, including significant events of his rule.
 
• It is an essential primary source for historians studying the Mughal period, offering insights into Jahangir's administration, personal life, and the socio-political scenario of the time.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inayat Khan**

 
 
• Inayat Khan was a noble in the court of Shah Jahan and wrote "Shah Jahan Nama," which chronicles the reign of Emperor Shah Jahan.
 
• His work provides insights into Shah Jahan's rule, including his architectural achievements and administrative measures.
 
 
 
• **Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan**
 
 
• Abdul Rahim was one of the Navaratnas (Nine Gems) in the court of Emperor Akbar and was known for his poetry, translation work, and patronage of arts.
 
• Though notable for his contributions, he did not write about Jahangir but was involved in translating "Baburnama" into Persian.
 
 
 
• **Abul Fazl**
 
 
• Abul Fazl was a close advisor of Emperor Akbar and one of the Navaratnas in his court.
 
• He authored the "Akbarnama," a three-volume history of Akbar's reign, and the "Ain-i-Akbari", which details the administrative system of the Mughal Empire.
 
• His comprehensive works are critical for understanding Akbar's imperial policies and governance.
